Why Math Dumped OpenAI
Don’t let anyone call the mathematicians Luddites. No.
AI in Math had a natural synergy that researchers made every effort to embrace. OpenAI turned this into a toxic relationship. This breakdown in trust runs parallel to what we see in Software Engineering and other domains.
When programmers say mathematicians are “feeling our pain” now, some mean it in the sense of being shocked to discover machines have surpassed them. That’s a naive but understandable take if you’ve seen recent headlines without prior knowledge of the situation. I’ll explain.
Calling a Spade a Spade
OpenAI’s position at the frontier of Mathematics is not that of the player making the biggest contribution, but of the player with the highest budget, biggest mouth, and least integrity.
The reason people call ChatGPT a “Super Intelligence,” but don’t consider Lean prover one, is that Sam Altman is a liar and Leonardo de Moura is not.
Lean FRO’s foundational contribution to these same breakthroughs has been more honest and more impactful, with a fraction of 1% of OpenAI’s resources. That’s just speaking of the part we could say “machines” are “doing,” which we normally speak of as results being formalized or mechanized.
One could argue that a statistical language engine is an inherently less honest technology than symbolic systems like Lean, but really they are mutually complementary. That’s not the problem. The problem is the billions of dollars being poured into a campaign to systematically dehumanize and devalue workers.
I like LLMs, the Large Language Models.
I don’t like LLMs, the Liar’s Layoff Machine.
You’re Never Enough
This is not an enemies-to-lovers story. This is a lovers-to-enemies story.
— Liz Martinez, co-host of The Coding Agency
There is no way to embrace AI.
This is a toxic relationship with an aggressor. Asking the aggrieved to “embrace change” will solve nothing. The reason AI Boosters are now met with hostility is because they are complicit in gaslighting.
I was an early adopter too. This is where it ends up. You can make every effort and it will never be enough, because it is not made for you.
Diagnosis
What I’m saying is that the AI Gold Rush exhibits the patterns of a narcissistic abuser.
I know what you’re wondering:
Ray, what could narcissism possibly have to do with companies founded on an inevitable God-like Super Intelligence so dangerous that no one else can be entrusted to create it, which should be the central focus of our global planning?
Good question. We’ll have to leave that as an exercise to the reader for now. Today’s post is a longitudinal case-study.
I’m not a medical professional and they don’t diagnose gold rushes, but under the DSM-5 criteria, the diagnosis of Narcissistic Personality Disorder requires 5 or more of these 9 traits.
- Grandiose sense of self-importance
- Frequent fantasies about having or deserving:
  - Success
  - Power
  - Intelligence
  - Beauty
  - Love
  - Self-fulfillment
- Belief in superiority
- Need for admiration
- Entitlement
- Willingness to exploit others
- Lack of empathy
- Frequent envy
- Arrogance
Does any of this sound familiar?
Flying Monkeys
Flying Monkeys are people under the influence of narcissists that act on their behalf by:
- Spreading lies and gossip
- Forming a shared fantasy
- Enabling abusive behavior by defending, dismissing, or excusing it
In this analogy, AI Boosters are Flying Monkeys. They might mean well, and are confused at how people react to their insistence that we make peace with the abuser (which, again, is impossible). They wonder how these Anti-AI people got so mean.
DARVO is an acronym for Deny, Attack, and Reverse Victim and Offender.
Professor Olivia Guest explains a DARVO example here. Her approach to critical AI literacy frequently draws this kind of attack. It’s a lopsided game where Machine Learning experts are taken more seriously about everyone else’s field, e.g. Cognitive Science.
Reactive abuse is intentionally triggering a reaction in order to blame the victim for aggression and make them seem like the problem.
Another tactic that pairs well here is to act like the conflict is literally with the machines no matter how many times we explain that we are criticizing specific people for their actions.
- Anthropic bans users from ‘needless abusive or cruel behavior’ towards Claude
- Anthropic Has Been Aggressively Lobbying the Vatican to Consider AI Consciousness
Not now, Dario, we’re trying to be serious.
Boundaries
Yet another group of domain experts is experiencing a trust breakdown with the US model labs.
The constituents are making their needs clear that things need to change. They are setting boundaries after numerous softer attempts failed.
This is the story of how the greatest ally of AI in Math wound up promoting these letters (signing the first).
- September 11th, 2026 - A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics signed by 25 Field’s medalists
- October 7th, 2026 - Statement on OpenAI’s October 6 Release of Mathematical Documents by Association for Human Mathematics (AHM)
No matter how the Flying Monkeys try to spin this, these are not people who merely fear change or automation. They are people supporting change for the better, criticizing change for the worse, and clearly explaining the difference.
The rest of this post will outline events that led to this as I followed them. I hope you find it helpful.
